Description

CGRP, released with substance P from peptidergic afferents, acts on a receptor made of the calcitonin receptor-like receptor and RAMP1. The receptor couples to Gs and raises cAMP. In the dorsal horn it lies mainly on presynaptic terminals, where it can modulate transmitter release. In OA models CGRP sensitises joint nociceptors to mechanical stimuli.

Colour

Each block is coloured by its effect on pain, red where it raises pain and blue where it relieves it, and everything in it takes that colour, GTP and GDP included, as it works for the block's result. Drugs are yellow and classes of molecules white.

This block is red: CGRP transmits nociceptive signals.

An intrathecal CGRP receptor antagonist relieves established OA pain, and CGRP8-37 reverses joint nociceptor sensitisation. On macrophages CGRP inhibits TNF (Feng 1997), the other way for inflammation.
